newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gunmen seize hostages near Chechnya - Russian media.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen seize hostages near Chechnya - Russian media.

text.p: Gunmen seized up to six people, some of them Chechens, as they travelled in a minibus near Russia's separatist region of Chechnya on Tuesday, Russian media reports said.

Itar-Tass news agency quoted regional security officials as saying six people, including five Chechens, were kidnapped close to the Chechen border as they travelled from the Caucasus region of North Ossetia to neighbouring Ingushetia.

NTV television also said six people had been seized but Interfax news agency quoted police officials in the region as saying witnesses had reported seeing only four people taken away. RIA news agency said five people had been kidnapped.
A spokeswoman at Russia's Emergencies Ministry said authorities were checking the reports. A Russian police spokesman in the region told Reuters by telephone that he knew nothing of the incident.
The agencies gave no further details about the identity of the hostages.
Tass said the minibus was stopped close to the North Ossetian town of Beslan by masked gunmen in two vehicles.
The empty minibus with Chechen registration plates was later found abandoned on the road, RIA said.

Hostage-taking has become a major problem in Chechnya, where Russian troops fought a bloody campaign against separatist forces for 21 months until last August, but kidnappings are rare in neighbouring regions.
Last week, two British aid workers were seized from the house where they were staying in Chechnya by masked gunmen.
Russian and foreign journalists and officials from the nearby Ingushetia and Ossetia regions have also been among those kidnapped in Chechnya in recent months. Some remain in captivity.
Chechen authorities said on Monday they were setting up a special mobile investigative unit, including judges of Islamic Sharia law, to tackle kidnappings in the region.
